rendered:
The anode-free full cell uses a presodiated pyrite (FeS2) cathode. Pyrite is chosen because it is a cheap, abundant material.[1][2] 
Because pyrite natively contains no sodium, it is sodiated before assembly. Cells are built from the presodiated pyrite paired with carbon/Al current collectors, in the discharged state. On the first charge, sodium ions leave the pyrite and are reduced on the carbon/Al collector to form sodium metal in situ, so the assembled cell has no sodium metal.[3][4][5][6] 
For the energy density (about 400[7] Wh/kg), the cathode capacity was assumed to be that of FeS2 at 335[8] mAh/g, with the presodiated pyrite taken as Na1.5FeS2 as the mass basis for the calculation.[9][10]
